Quick technical summary / options for the reply: 

Option A — Redwood-managed keys (default)
- Description: Redwood holds encryption keys, manages key rotation, audit logging.
- Pros: fastest onboarding, no cross-account KMS setup, lower latency (no cross-account calls during tokenization).
- Cons: customer may not accept for PHI; less control for customer; we provide exportable audit logs and CA-based attestations.
- Compliance: works with SOC 2; for HIPAA we execute a BAA but many customers require CMEK for PHI in production.

Option B — Customer-managed keys in AWS KMS (recommended middle path)
- Description: Customer creates a KMS key in their AWS account (HSM-backed), grants Redwood a minimal IAM principal / cross-account decrypt permission for envelope keys. Redwood stores only encrypted envelope keys.
- Pros: strong customer control, HSM-backed keys, full key rotation under customer control, auditability via CloudTrail.
- Cons: adds cross-account setup and onboarding steps; minimal latency impact (one KMS Decrypt during envelope key wrap/unwrap, cache envelope keys per-session to avoid per-token KMS calls).
- Implementation notes: use envelope encryption — generate data encryption keys (DEKs) per model session, DEKs encrypted by customer CMK. Cache DEKs in Redis KV cache with tight TTL and enforce strict entropy and rotation policies. Document cross-account IAM roles and a short-runbook.

Option C — External HSM / BYOK with CloudHSM or on-prem HSM gateway
- Description: Keys live in a dedicated HSM and Redwood calls an HSM gateway for crypto operations.
- Pros: maximum control, compliance-heavy customers prefer this; keys never leave HSM.
- Cons: significant operational complexity, networking (VPN/VPC) setup, latency increases for synchronous operations, potentially higher cost and longer procurement timeline.

Risk & observations:
- Auditability: ensure CloudTrail + Redwood's token-level audit traces are correlated (timestamp + request-id).
- Rotation: recommend quarterly rotation for DEK, yearly rotation for CMK unless customer policy dictates otherwise.
- Latency: envelope approach minimizes per-token latency — only DEK unwrap at session start. Make sure to document cache invalidation on rotation.
- Logging & key usage: require KMS/CloudHSM key usage logs to be shared or accessible by Medisure for audits.

Recommendation for Medisure pilot:
- Pilot on Option B (Customer-managed AWS KMS). It's the fastest to implement with strong auditability and acceptable latency. Pilot with non-production PHI-like data and a BAA in place. If they require stronger guarantees post-pilot, evaluate Option C.

Attachments: I exported a short matrix (cmk-implementation-options.xlsx) for the external reply that outlines configurations and ownership responsibilities.

1) Documentation handoff: we will send SOC 2 Type II under NDA to security@medisure.health and provide our standard DPA + BAA draft links. (See HubSpot deal & doc link below.)

2) Recommended pilot config (low-friction, HIPAA-ready): Option B — Customer-managed keys in your AWS account (HSM-backed KMS CMK) using envelope encryption. Summary: Redwood will only hold encrypted DEKs; we will perform a cross-account KMS decrypt at session start and cache DEKs for the session lifetime to avoid per-token KMS calls. This preserves customer key control and provides CloudTrail auditability.

3) Alternative (if Medisure prefers maximum custody): Option C — External HSM gateway / CloudHSM. This requires additional networking and procurement lead time; we can scope it in parallel if you'd like.

4) Pilot checklist & timeline: 
- Sign NDA & BAA (we can attach initial drafts).
- Medisure to provision CMK in AWS and grant Redwood a restricted decrypt role (we will provide Terraform snippets and a minimal IAM guide).
- Schedule 45-min technical deep-dive (Marcus + Aditya + Medisure infra) — proposed slots: Wed Apr 7 10:00am PT or Thu Apr 8 2:00pm PT.

Please confirm: 1) if Option B is acceptable for the pilot, and 2) preferred slot for the deep-dive. Once confirmed, Marcus will join the call to walk through the IAM, CloudTrail requirements, and runbook.

Thanks — Camila
